physical_harm: Injuries caused to complainant, his father, brother and mother-in-law, leading to the death of the brother
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the evidence that the accused persons did not allow the injured to come out from their house for about three hours, preventing them from receiving medical treatment, which led to the death of the complainant's brother.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as credible, noting that all eye-witnesses assigned the role of all the accused in causing injuries, and that minor inconsistencies in their statements do not make their evidence unreliable.
bail_history: Bail bonds of all accused persons stand cancelled.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 12.11.1993; Trial judgment: 08.10.2002; High Court decision: 21.12.2005; Supreme Court decision: APRIL21,2017
legal_representation: Ms. Smita Hazarika, Adv. for the appellants; Debojit Borkakati and Shuvodeep Roy, Advs. for the respondent
investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed
appeal_history: Outcome at trial court: Convicted under Section 302 r/w 149 IPC; Outcome at High Court: Appeal dismissed; Outcome at Supreme Court: Appeal dismissed
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused persons armed with various weapons attacked the complainant, his father, brother and mother-in-law, and after inflicting injuries, did not allow the injured to be taken to hospital for about 3 hours, resulting in the complainant's brother's death. The trial court convicted the accused under Section 302 r/w 149 IPC and sentenced them to life imprisonment.
defence_argument: The defence contended that the FIR mentioned only five accused persons, whereas the charge sheet was submitted against twelve accused, and there were contradictions in the evidence of eye-witnesses. They argued that the non-mention of other accused in the FIR indicated they could not have been convicted.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that it is unreasonable to expect a witness to give a picture perfect report of the incident and that minor discrepancies in their statement have to be ignored.
precedent_relied_upon: Chandrappa and Others v. State of Karnataka (2008) 11 SCC 328
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed due to the clear evidence of the accused persons' involvement in the attack, their role in preventing the injured from receiving medical treatment, and the common object of the unlawful assembly leading to the death of the complainant's brother.
judicial_aggravating_factors: The court weighed the aggravating factors of the accused persons' role in preventing the injured from receiving medical treatment, which led to the death of the complainant's brother, and their involvement in an unlawful assembly with a common object of assault.
